clue.text: Sacked king of Bashan's log-carriers

parts.note: to be sacked is to be fired from a job
Og was the giant king of Bashan in the Old Testament; with the possessive he gives OGS

explanation.surface: A dismissed biblical king's servants who carried his firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: Og, king of Bashan, is a biblical giant (Deuteronomy 3). Firedogs are the metal stands that hold logs in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Andirons in a hearth support burning logs, so they literally carry the logs.

clue.text: Starve if ham's gone bad

indicators.note: meat that has gone bad is spoiled and changed, so the letters of these words are reworked

parts.note: the possessive 's still gives an S here: the letters taken are those of ham's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone would rather go hungry than eat ham that has turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone bad' rearranges the letters of IF HAMS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to make or be extremely hungry, the same as to go without food.

clue.text: Income received by letter

parts.note: a 'letter' here is not mail but one who lets property, a landlord, and the money such a person takes in is the sum paid by tenants

explanation.surface: Money arriving through the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made by a tenant to a landlord for the use of property is exactly a landlord's income.

clue.text: Dishonest cutie fled in confusion

indicators.note: being in confusion means being jumbled up, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pretty but untrustworthy person ran off in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful and dishonest are synonyms describing someone given to lying or trickery.

clue.text: Act in accordance with management, but get neglected

definitions.meaning: read literally, to follow what the board of directors says
the idiom for being abandoned or ignored, from things thrown overboard

explanation.surface: An employee obeys the bosses yet is overlooked anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase means following the board's lead; idiomatically it means to be discarded or left aside.

clue.text: Come out on top with increased yield

parts.note: a crop is the yield of a field at harvest
figures that have increased are said to be up

explanation.surface: A farmer comes out best with a bigger harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out on top' reads as one phrase, but only 'Come out' is the definition; 'on top with' just joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: When a matter appears unexpectedly it is said to arise or surface, which is the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: Cecil's sound means of communication

indicators.note: sound here means as heard, so a name spoken out is taken for a word spelt differently

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was the Victorian empire-builder; the possessive points to his surname

explanation.surface: Cecil's dependable way of keeping in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it signals that RHODES, Cecil's surname, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Highways link towns and let people and goods travel, a basic channel of communication.

clue.text: Underground explorer a menace in the kitchen ?

definitions.meaning: a caver who goes down shafts and caves
read whimsically, someone who punches holes in cooking pans

explanation.surface: A caver who is a disaster when cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A caver descends into pot-holes; the joke reading is one who makes holes in pans, wrecking cookware.

clue.text: Principles of local taxation

definitions.meaning: in Britain, demands issued by one authority to another for a share of local rates

explanation.surface: The guiding rules of council tax.
explanation.walkthrough: In British local government a precept is the levy one authority (a county, a parish) asks the rate-collecting council to raise for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Precepts are moral rules; in the British rating system they are also levy demands for local tax.

clue.text: Vehicles constitute CBI's main problem

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so these letters are put through a rearrangement

parts.note: the possessive 's gives an S; the letters used are those of CBIs

explanation.surface: The Confederation of British Industry's chief worry is taxi cabs.
explanation.walkthrough: The CBI is the Confederation of British Industry, a UK business lobby. 'problem' rearranges CBIS plus MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Minicabs are small hire cars, a kind of road transport.

clue.text: Power unit completed with the French building material

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An electrical unit is paired with a French article to make construction stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completed with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is woven twigs used, with daub, to make walls of huts and old houses.

clue.text: Dignified Australians with parts in Hamlet

parts.note: grave means solemn and dignified
digger is an informal term for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: Stately actors from Australia have roles in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two clowns digging Ophelia's grave are characters in Shakespeare's play, so they are roles in it.

clue.text: Indian teacher was confused by motorway

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so the short word before it is rearranged

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway; the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A guru got lost on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges WAS into SWA; the M1 runs from London to Leeds, its 1 standing in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Bird changes colour

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Something alters its hue.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a shore wader named for flipping pebbles to find food.

clue.text: Bubbly effects never achieved by new make

indicators.note: giving these letters a new make means building them afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Fizzy results were never managed by a new brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new make' rearranges EFFECTS plus NEVER; 'achieved by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Effervescent means fizzing with gas bubbles, or lively in manner.

clue.text: Sri Lanka man has inspiration in the south-east

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the abbreviation being split around the verb

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
inspiration is breathing in, so someone who has it inhales

explanation.surface: A man from Sri Lanka finds his muse in the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' means a breath, not a creative idea: INHALES goes between S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinhalese are the majority ethnic group of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Like Macpherson's epic manner

parts.note: James Macpherson published epic poems in the 1760s that he claimed were by an ancient Gaelic bard, and the adjective describes their grandiose style

explanation.surface: Imitating the style of a Scottish poet's epic.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the bard Macpherson invented, or the inflated bombastic style of those poems.

clue.text: Vehicles it will carry, including French railway material

definitions.text: Vehicles it will carry, including French railway material

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, the French word placed between its letters

parts.note: fer is French for iron, the metal rails are made of, as in chemin de fer

explanation.surface: A vessel that carries motor vehicles, perhaps a rail-linked boat with iron fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: Fer is iron, the metal of rails. The whole clue also describes the vessel: it carries cars (and, on train ferries, railway stock).
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to carry motor vehicles across water is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Little investment in restricted growth area

parts.note: little means small
a holding is an investment, such as a holding of shares

explanation.surface: A minor stake put into a dwarfism zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted growth' suggests dwarfism, but here it is land of limited size for growing crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A smallholding is a small plot of farmland, an area where cultivation is limited in scale.

clue.text: Stupid, one variety of this game

definitions.text: Stupid, one variety of this game

parts.words: Stupid, one variety of this game
parts.note: stupid is read as dumb, and the dumb version of this rhyming parlour game, acted out in mime, is a known variety

explanation.surface: An insult, then a note that this pastime has several forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb crambo is a miming variant of the rhyming word game, so dumb is one variety of it.

clue.text: Travelled by air, not by motor

definitions.text: Travelled by air, not by motor

parts.words: Travelled by air, not by motor
parts.note: describes flight without an engine, as a sailplane does on rising air currents

explanation.surface: Someone flew without an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding is flying without engine power, borne on air currents.

clue.text: Turned out fine, so all sails hoisted !

definitions.meaning: a ship carrying every sail it has

explanation.surface: The weather cleared up, so the ship spread all its canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out fine' looks like weather talk, but it means smartly dressed; 'so' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is nautical for a ship carrying every sail, and colloquially means dressed up in one's best clothes.

clue.text: Nail up a climber

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top, read backwards

explanation.surface: Hammer a nail upward into a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAIL into LIAN, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine that climbs up forest trees.

clue.text: Girl may have trouble about public relations

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: A young woman might struggle with publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Standard pattern a student follows

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the learner letter is placed after the rest

parts.note: a norm is a standard pattern of behaviour
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A pupil copies the usual model.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plates displayed by learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual, conforming to the standard.

clue.text: Saved from being paid off

definitions.meaning: a debt or mortgage cleared by payment

explanation.surface: Rescued once the debt was cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from being' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem is both to rescue a soul in religious language and to clear a debt or reclaim a pledge by payment.

clue.text: Alligator goes from islet to isle

parts.note: a cay is a low small island or reef
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A reptile swims from one small island to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes from ... to' simply links the two islands in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The caiman is a Central and South American relative of the crocodile in the alligator family.

clue.text: Eros, such a heavenly body !

parts.note: seems to praise the god of love's physique, but Eros is also a minor planet that comes close to Earth

explanation.surface: Admiring the god of love's gorgeous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is a near-Earth minor planet orbiting the Sun, one of many rocky bodies so classed.
